einzeiler: How the Radium Girls fought corporate lies and shaped modern labor safety standards.
kurzfassung: During and after World War I, female watch dial painters exposed to radioactive paint suffered horrific health consequences while employers denied responsibility. Led by Grace Fryer, the surviving workers fought back through medical testing and landmark lawsuits. Their courageous battle exposed corporate negligence and laid the groundwork for modern workplace safety regulations.
stichpunkte: Factory workers painted watch dials with radium paint and were taught to lip-point their brushes.
Radium was widely celebrated as a miracle cure and health booster before its dangers were known.
Workers began suffering severe health issues, including deteriorating jaws, bone pain, and mysterious deaths initially misdiagnosed as syphilis.
Medical examiners developed groundbreaking breath and radiation tests that definitively linked the illnesses to radium ingestion.
Victims faced corporate suppression, victim-blaming, and legal hurdles regarding statutes of limitations.
Grace Fryer led a group of former dial painters in filing a high-profile lawsuit against their employer in 1928.
Key figures faced their own radiation-related illnesses, leading to dramatic courtroom twists and a eventual settlement.
The legal fight and international attention helped establish worker protections and contributed to the creation of OSHA.
beschreibung:
September 12, 1922. Twenty-four-year-old Mollie Maggia has a toothache. In less than a year, this otherwise healthy young woman will be dead. Others like her will soon follow. They’d all shared what seemed to be a dream job: applying glow-in-the-dark paint to clock faces. The paint glowed because it was saturated with radium, the wonder element of its day. And now that radium has burrowed inside the bones and lungs of the women. How did a supposed wonder element and cure-all come to be seen for what it was – a deadly poison? And how did a group of courageous young women, racing the clock of their own mortality, expose this truth?
Special thanks to Kate Moore, author of The Radium Girls: The Dark Story of America’s Shining Women. Also, a huge thank you to Art Fryer, nephew of Grace Fryer, one of the “Radium Girls.”
